The Steinheimer and Ries craters in the west of this region are believed to have been created by the impact of a binary asteroid, and its city of Ergolding was destroyed during the Landshut War of Succession. The Allgau mountain range is located in the south of this state, and the control of one of its ruling houses was ended via the Anif Declaration. The Agilolfings ruled this region until their last ruler, Tassilo III, was deposed by Charlemagne, and the founder of its capital, Henry the Lion, was a member of the House of Guelph who was deposed by Frederick Barbarossa. This state contains its nation's highest peak, Zugspitze, and its cities include Regensburg, Augsburg and Nuremburg. Its ► Neuschwanstein Castle was built by Mad King Ludwig, and this state's capital was the site of the Beer Hall Putsch. Bordered by Hesse, Saxony and Baden-Wurttemberg, name this largest state of Germany, with capital at Munich.

This site lies on the Pulwar River, and was partly cut out of the nearby Mountain of Mercy. When this city dwindled in power, nearby Estakhr overtook it in importance, and Tachara and Hadish are among the minor palaces at this site. Ernst Herzfeld, the first European to excavate this, believed that its purpose was to celebrate Nowruz, and planning of the nearby Sivand Dam has been met with protest out of fear that it would damage this site, as well as nearby Pasargadae. Nearby Naqsh-e Rustam served as a tomb for several rulers, and this site's Gate of All Nations opened up to the Apadana Palace. Located in the Fars Province, which has its capital at ► Shiraz, this site is sometimes known as the thrown of Yima or Jamshid, a shepherd who was made king by Ahura Mazda. Destroyed by a fire started by the army of Alexander the Great, name this ancient city of Iran which served as the ceremonial capital of Achaemenid Persia.

The Berger-Parker and Shannon-Wiener indices are used to measure this, although the Simpson method is more common, and Rapoport's Rule states that this is smaller at low latitudes than high ones. Edward O. Wilson uses the acronym HIPPO to simplify the threats to this, and Facilitation is an effect of high rates of it. The Svalbard ► Seed Vault's purpose is to preserve this in case of global catastrophe, and lack of this is what caused Phytophthora infestans to be so devastating during the Irish Potato Blight, sometimes called monoculture. Name this term of ecology which refers to the variation of flora and fauna within a given ecosystem.

This body of water's namesake national recreation area features Cochran Shoals, and is where it meets its tributary Vickery Creek, and its namesake bay is separated from the Gulf of Mexico by the islands of St. George, St. Vincent and Dog. This river forms the ACF Basin with its largest tributary, the Flint River, which it meets in Lake Seminole, and this body of water was the subject of an epic poem by Sidney Lanier. Flowing past Columbus and the suburbs of ► Atlanta, name this river which creates much of the Georgia/Alabama border and is known as the Apalachicola while in Florida.

Drained by the Jupiter River, Lake Wickenden is the largest of this island, and its most populous town is Port-Menier. Along with the nearby Mingan Archipelago, this island was owned solely by Louis Jollet for a time, and troops of William Phips occupied it during King William's War. The Honguedo Strait separates this from the Gaspe Peninsula, while the Jacques Cartier Strait separates it from Labrador. For 20 points, name this sparsely populated island in the middle of the Gulf of Saint Lawrence, controlled by Quebec.

The chief deity of these people's mythology, also known as the Lady of Anboto, is served by the Sorginaks, and her consort is Sugaar. These people worshipped the aforementioned Mari until their conversion to Christianity, and their native land includes the Urkiola and Aralar mountain ranges. Gassia Semen was a leader of these people who began a revolt in the 9th century, and their lands had earlier been incorporated into the Banu Qasi, which had its capital at Tudela. Their largest city is centered on the Nervion River, and until recently, Jurdan Martitegi led a terrorist organization of these peoples known as the ETA. The Alava, Guipuzcoa and Biscay provinces make up their home region, whose cities include Vitoria, ► Guernica and Bilbao. The victors of the Battle of Roncevaux Pass over the forces of Roland, name these people of southern France and northern Spain who speak a non-Indo-European language and created Jai alai.

A quarry near this city has recently been turned into the Ngomongo Villages and Haller Park, and its suburbs include Bamburi and Likoni. Supposedly founded by Shehe Mvita, the Portuguese founded Fort Jesus at the site of this city, and it is separated by the Port Reitz and Tudor creeks from the mainland. In the harbor of this city, Venus and some nymphs save sailors from the treachery of Bacchus in The Lusiads, shortly after da Gama's ships have been poorly received at nearby Kilwa. Connected to the mainland by Nyali Bridge and the Makupa Causeway, this city features ► Kilindini Harbor and is served by Moi International Airport. Located on its namesake island in the Indian Ocean, name this major port city of Kenya.

The Door Peninsula helped create this region by blocking the Superior lobe and some remnant species in this area include the Pleistocene Disk and the Northern Blue Monkshood. This region is the only known area of the world to feature the Algific talus slope ecosystem which uses sinkholes and talus-covered slopes to produce a windy, extra-cool environment. Military Ridge forms the southern end of this area, and the Baraboo range forms the eastern border of it. For 20 points, identify this area of the Midwest, primarily in southwestern Wisconsin, that was never covered by glaciers during the last ice age.

This province contains Accona Desert as well as the Crete senesi which is home to the Monte Oliveto Maggiore monastery. Metals and borax are mined in this province's Maremma district and Alpi Apuane is a major quarry for Carrara marble. The Pratomagno is a large mountain range in this area and this region's Chianti district is known for its wine, while the town of San Gimignano is famous for its towers, and the town of ► Siena is known for its horse race. Val di Chiana drains into Umbria from this province which also contains the more famous Val d'Orsina. Identify this region through which the Arno River flows.

A valley called Joey's Garden on this island leads to Ridge-Where-the-Goat-Jumps-Off while East and West Jew's Point commemorate the recovery of a Jew rescued from a ship. One of this island's dependencies is Inaccessible Island, which has a noted flightless bird, and Gough Island serves as a source of Guano for inhabitants of this island. A massive fire in early 2008 destroyed this island's power generators and fishing factory and an unexpected cinder cone eruption in 1961 destroyed parts of the major settlement, Edinburgh of the Seven Seas. For 20 points, identify this small island in the South Atlantic Ocean, a dependency of St. Helena.

Bertram Thomas was the first European to cross this region, and Iram of the Pillars is a legendary city of the people of 'Ad at the site of a collapsed limestone cavern in it. St. John Philby searched in this area but only ended up finding freshwater clam shells and hippo teeth in the Mudafan sector, and there are several meteor craters at Al-Hadidah. Bounded on the east by the Hajar Mountains and the west by the Asir Mountains, many caravan routes crossed this from the Frankincense-producing areas near Salalah. The Shaybah field is located on the northern edge of this area, while further to the west in this region is the Ghawwar oil field, which is the world's largest. For 15 points, identify this desert located in northern Yemen and Oman as well as southeastern Saudi Arabia, sometimes called The Empty Quarter.

The Garibaldi and Anaheim Volcanic Belts are located in this region, and volcanoes formed such landmarks as Mount Meager and the Level Mountain Range here. The Okanagon region is this province's primary wine-producing region, and the towns of Hudson's Hope and Kamloops are located in it. The Haida Heritage site is located in this province where the Kootenay River rises before it flows across a national border and back again, and the Stikine Plateau is located at the center of this province which also includes ► Yoho National Park, the site of the famous Burgress Shale formation. The Frazer valley cuts through much of what Canadian province whose capital sits on Vancouver Island?

South of this city is the Ukok Plateau and Salair Ridge, as well as a man-made lake polluted by nuclear waste. One part of this city, Akademgorodok, is an area called the "Silicon Forest" and is home to the "House of the Scientists," a major center for scientific research which was allegedly the site where perestroika was conceived. The Kommunalniy Bridge replaced the original span that prompted this city's founding in 1893 and this city celebrated the introduction of its first Metro in 1985. For 15 points, identify this third-largest city in Russia, located on the Ob River and the Trans-Siberian Railway.

The Maah Daah Hey single track bike trail, the longest in the US, is located in this state and this state's endoheric Devil's Lake has been controversially rerouted into the Sheyenne River. The Canonnball and Knife rivers are located in this state and The International Peace Garden is located in this state's Turtle Mountain region. The Souris River basin is located in this state's Drift Prairie area, and its highest point, White Butte, is located near the Kildeer Mountains. Garrison Dam created Lake Sakakewa in this state and the Elkhorn Ranch is located in ► Theodore Roosevelt National Park, which also contains part of the Badlands. Identify this state bisected by the Missouri River whose eastern border is formed by the Red River.

Carstensz Pyramid is the highest point on this island and it was named for Dutch explorer ridiculed for claiming to have seen snow on this island. The Fly River system on this island was majorly affected by the Ok Tedi mine's tailings and the Sepik River originates in the Victor Emmanuel Range before flowing into the Bismarck Sea. The Owen Stanley Mountains block off access to the only national capital on this island and Jayapura is the largest city within another province on this island. Daru is located on the northern side of the ► Torres Strait which separates this island from the Cape York Peninsula to the south. Identify this island nation where over 800 different languages are spoken.

The Adal, Aussa, and Harar sultanates existed in this region prior to European colonization, and cities here include Assab and Kismaayo. Ras Xaafun is the easternmost point of this region, and its lowest point is Lake Abbe, located on the border of two of its nations. The Dahlak Archipelago and the island of Socotra lie off this, and it is bordered by the Massawa Channel and Gulf of Tadjoura. The Bale and Semien Mountains make up the backbone of this region, and its sub-regions include Afar, Ogaden and Puntland. Lying between the ► Gulf of Aden, the larger Red Sea, and the Indian Ocean, name this eastern region of a certain continent, on which lies the nations of Eritrea, Djibouti, Ethiopia and Somalia.

Kalambaka and Kastraki are the closest villages to this location, and one structure at this location was built by Athanasios Koinovitis on the Broad Rock. Another structure at this site contains several frescoes by Theophanes the Cretan, and Varlaam is the only nunnery on this site. The head of St. Charalambos can be found at this site, and a new bridge has made access to Roussanou much easier. The Agia Triada at this site was used in a James Bond movie, and although there were originally 24 monasteries at this site, only six survive. For 20 points, identify this site at the edge of the Pindus Mountains where Orthodox Greek monasteries appear to float in the air.

Robert Frost intended to commit suicide here after being rejected by some girl, but was rescued by a group of hunters instead. A lake in this area has very high amounts of tannin and most of this area is contained within Gates, Perquimans, and Camden counties. Erik Prince built a compound in this area that later grew into a multinational mercenary company, and Lake Drummond lies in its center. George Washington suggested draining this area by constructing a canal, although the existing canals, such as the Jericho and Railroad ditches functioned as conduits for lumber. Harriet Beecher Stowe's second novel, ► Dred, is subtitled after this swamp, and describes how runaway slaves hid in it. Identify this massive marshy region that covers much of southeastern Virginia and northeastern North Carolina.

One of these called SarisariÃ±ama is famous for its perfectly round sinkholes and one called Autana has a cave that runs completely from one side of it through to the other. Parts of them are extremely nutrient-poor which include insectivores like Drosera roraimae and Urticularia humboldtii and nearly one third of all plant species located on them are endemic. One group of them is called Los Testigos and Abismo Guy Collet, the deepest quartzite cave in the world, is found in one of these, and their tops are famous sites for fulgurites. Many of these are located in the Gran Sabana and one called Matawi is sacred to the local Peton Indians while Cuquenan Falls is located on another. Many of these are located in Canaima National Park and Monte Roraima may be the most famous. For 20 points, identify these large flat-topped mountains located in the Guinea Highlands of South America.

Mark Twain describes this geographical feature in Chapters 38 through 39 of "Roughing It" where he claimed it could launder clothes within minutes. This lake avoided the fate of nearby Owens Lake after an extensive lawsuit, and this lake's Navy Beach is the site of an old naval installation, while Panum Crater looms over this lake's south shore. Fed by Rush creek, the waters of this lake harbor huge populations of brine shrimp and brine flies, making it an important nesting spot for the California Gull. Large towers of tufa dot the shoreline as well as the Negit isles and Pahoa Island, and this lake is located on a volcano chain just north of the Long Valley Caldera. For 15 points, identify this lake located between the Inyo and Sierra Nevada mountains, the largest lake found entirely within California.

In the Mutou Valley of this region lie the Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves near the ancient ruins of Gaochang, and a highway has recently been constructed across this to connect the cities of Luntai and Hotan on its edges. This region's name translates as "Go in and you'll never come out," and its cities of Marin and Yarkand were key oases along the Silk Road. A part of the Tarim Basin, for 15 points, name this region lying between the Kunlun, Pamir and Tien Shan mountain ranges, a desert located in the Xinjiang Uyghur region of western China.

In the 17th century, a stretch of this river's bank, Biffeche, was ruled by a chief known as the Little King, who had his capital at Maka. In 1972, the OMVS was set up by four nations to regulate this, and its flow is stopped by the Maka-Diama and Manantali dams. This waterway passes through the Talari Gorges before creating the Gouina Falls, both in the Kayes Region, and its tributaries include the Faleme, Karakoro and Gorgol rivers. Before reaching the ocean, this river skirts the Langue de Barbarie, an almost 400 mile long peninsula of sand, and finally reaches its mouth at Saint-Louis. Formed by the confluence of the Bafing and Semefe, or Bakoy, rivers in Bafoulabe, like the Gambia and Niger rivers, this waterway begins in ► Guinea. Identify this African river which separates Mauritania from its namesake nation with capital at Dakar.

He succeeded Jean Jacques Berger in one position, and was in charge of a department named for a prominent river. This man was influenced by the work of Ildefons Cerda, and Walter Benjamin's Arcades Project came about because of his work. This man was dismissed by Emile Ollivier and attacked in a pamphlet by Jules Ferry. The designs of this man are prominently featured in a painting that also features some ► umbrellas and rain, a work by Gustave Caillebotte. This man worked on the Boulogne Woods, but is better known for his barricades and wide boulevards in a prominent European capital. Name this 19th century urban planner who helped Napoleon III redesign Paris during the years of the Second Empire.

Popular landmarks at this location include the "Bridge of 72 Hours," so-named because it was built within that time span, and the tallest flagpole in the world. Violent actions that have occurred at this site include the assault perpetrated on W.D. Henderson in 1975 and the "axe murders" which killed Arthur Bonifas and Paul Barrett in 1976. A twenty foot stump of a poplar tree can be found at this location as a reminder of Operation Paul Bunyan, which consisted of a large task force assigned to cut down the offending structure. Other structures found at this location include the "Bridge of No Return," where Operation Big Switch took place and which was notably traversed by Lloyd Bucher and his crew in 1968. Tourists may visit the Third Tunnel of Aggression, which burrows underneath this location, and a place known as ► "Peace Village," which is suspected to be an uninhabited site used for propaganda purposes, is found here. Featuring such towns as Tae Sung Dong and Panmunjeom, identify this strip of land created in 1953 along the 38th parallel, a highly militarized area that separates two Asian countries.

The Balsas River forms part of this state's western border, and the cities of Ixtapa and Taxco are two of the cities in its Triangle of the Sun, a tourism hotspot. In pre-Colombian times, the Tarascans were centered northwest of this region in the state of Michoacan, and their leader, Caltzontzin, frequently visited this region's city of Zihuatanejo. At an 1813 congress in its capital, Jose Morelos outlined his Sentiments of the Nation, and a plan named after this region's city of Iguala, also known as the Plan of the Three Guarantees, was a peace treaty between Agustin de Iturbide and this state's namesake. The diving cliffs of La Quebrada are an attraction in this state's most notable city, which served Spain as the port from which their galleons traveled to and from ► Manila. With capital at Ciudad Bravo or Chilpancingo, name this Mexican state bordered by Oaxaca, Morelos, Puebla and the Pacific Ocean, whose largest city is Acapulco.

During World War One, Ukrainian immigrants were sent to internment camps at this location's Castle Mountain, and its namesake longnose dace went extinct over twenty years ago. The Sawback Range stretches into the northwest corner of this park, which includes Vermilion Lakes. This park's Moraine Lake is situated in the Valley of the Ten Peaks, and its Wapta Icefield is the source of the Bow River. The glacial Lake Louise is a notable feature of this park, which is located adjacent to Yoho and Kootenay national parks, and connected by the Icefields Parkway to ► Jasper National Park. Located around 100 miles west of Calgary in the Rocky Mountains, name this Alberta landmark, the oldest national park in Canada.

The first settlements near this body of water were set up by people who worshipped Mareiwa and Pulowi and who were known as the Wayuu. Islands found on this lake include Zapara, San Carlos, and Toas, and Lagunetas is a notable example of the palafitos on this body of water. On July 24, 1823, a major naval battle was fought on this lake, with Admiral Padilla defeating royalist forces, a date celebrated as a regional holiday by the Zulia state, where this lake is found. The Catatumbo River flows into this, and a bridge spanning the outlet of this lake was designed by Riccardo Morandi and is named after a military figure in the country's history, General Rafael ►Urdaneta. Name this large South American lake, which is actually a bay, and which shares its name with the second-largest city in Venezuela.

Bo Jonsson was the first owner of one castle in this archipelago, which is thought to have been the farthest extent to which the Comb Ceramic culture spread in the west. This archipelago was transferred to one nation via the Treaty of Hamina, and its only land border is on the skerry of Market. Ytternas, Langnas and Berghamn are among the main ports of this archipelago, whose main island is Fasta. The Bomarsund Fortress on these islands was destroyed during the Crimean War, and they were demilitarized in the ensuing Treaty of Paris. With capital at Mariehamn and lying at the entrance of the Gulf of Bothnia, for 15 points, identify this autonomous Swedish-speaking archipelago of Finland.

This body of water has one branch that begins at Okamanpeedan Lake, while the more northerly branch begins at Lake Shetek, and the two meet in Frank Gotch State Park. This river was named after the Otoe tribe when it first appeared on maps, and it is dammed to create the Red Rock and Saylorville reservoirs. Although the vast majority of this river's length lies in one state, some cities in the other state that this river flows by are Currie and Windom, while in its main state, it flows past Algona, Chillicothe, Fort Dodge and Ottumwa. The Raccoon River empties into this river at the downtown of this river's namesake city, and it forms a small part of the border between two Midwestern states that fought a bloodless 1839 conflict called the Honey War. Emptying into the Mississippi at Keokuk, name this river which forms part of Missouri's western border and shares its name with the capital of Iowa.

According to oral traditions of nearby cultures, men once saved themselves from being sacrificed if they journeyed to this location, which they called Enen-kio, to obtain the wing bone of a seabird found on it. In 1935, a village named "PAAville" was constructed at this location by Pan-American Airlines as a stopover on its US-China route. One notable incident in its history occurred in 1866, when an English opera troupe was stranded here after their ship, the Libelle, was wrecked off its eastern reef and this location once named "San Francisco" by its European discoverer, Alvaro de Mendana de Neyra. Books about this location include histories written by James Devereux and Winfield Cunningham, the latter of which once said "Send us more Japs!" in response to a failed landing during World War Two, and Admiral Shigematsu Sakaibara was later executed for ordering a 1943 massacre of American prisoners of war here. Featuring Wilkes and Peale Islands, which both surround a central lagoon, identify this atoll which takes its name from its largest island, the site of a December 1941 battle sometimes called the "Alamo of the Pacific."

Tourist destinations in this state include the Belum Caves and Horsley Hills, and the Kuchipudi is a dance which originates from it. This state surrounds the enclave of Yanam, which belongs to Pondicherry, and it was the target of Operation Polo because Asaf Jah VII, its last Nizam, chose not to become part of India. Kakinada and Visakhapatnam are the chief ports of this state, and its two main rivers are the Krishna and the Godavari. The Vijavanagar once ruled from this state, and the ancient ruins of Golconda lie in it. Bordered by the states of Karnataka and Orissa and lying on the ► Bay of Bengal, name this Telugu-speaking Indian state with capital at Hyderabad, which is not to be confused with the similarly named states of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

A cave called Devil's Kitchen and a rock called Sugar Loaf can be found at this location, while the "father of gastric physiology," William Beaumont performed his initial experiments on Alexis St. Martin here in 1822. This island was the site of the second national park in the United States, which later became its namesake state park, and it once served as the center of John Jacob Astur's American Fur Company. A 1947 film starring Esther Williams and Jimmy Durante, This Time for Keeps, was filmed at this location, as was a romance starring Christopher Reeve and Jane Seymour, Somewhere in Time. According to native legend, ► Michabou created this location and it served as the home of the Great Spirit known as the Gitche Manitou. Featuring Fort Holmes, which was named for a casualty during an 1814 battle fought at this site, this location is noted for its delicious fudge and its draconian anti-automobile laws. Identify this noted tourist destination, an island located in its namesake strait between the upper and lower peninsulas of Michigan.

A children's library in this city is named after the author of Tambores en la Noche, the black poet Jorge Artel. Centenary Park, built to commemorate a century of independence, can be found in this city's Getsemani Neighborhood. At the end of the Dique Canal in this city, ethnologist Gerardo Reichel-Dolmatoff discovered settlements belonging to the Monsu culture, which created artificial mounds that apparently were communal huts. This city features a monument to a woman named "India Catalina," who worked as the interpreter for Pedro de Heredia. In this city's Santo Domingo Square there can be found the sculpture Mujer Reclinada by Fernando Botero, and it is served by an airport named after a leader of the La Regeneracion movement, Rafael Nunez. This city was assaulted by the French and their buccaneer allies in a bloody 1697 incident during the War of the Grand Alliance, and later, a huge British force under ► Admiral Vernon failed to take this city during the War of Jenkin's Ear. Named after a port in Murcia, identify this port city of Colombia which gives its name to an 1812 manifesto written by Simon Bolivar.

This mountain has been painted by such artists as Mabel Moores Frisbee and Harry Cassie Best. Glaciers on this mountain include the Hotlum and Wintun, while local mythology claims that the spirit chief Skell lives on this peak. The first reliable sighting of this peak is credited to fur trapper Peter Skene Ogden, who gave it its name, although French explorer La Perouse claimed to have seen its last eruption. Frederick Spencer Oliver's A Dweller on Two Planets claims that Lemurians lived inside this mountain, and this forms a National Forest named after itself and the nearby Trinity Alps. Located in Siskiyou County, this peak's namesake river is a tributary of the Klamath, and the 1975 Summit Lighthouse Conference run by Elizabeth Clare Prophet met at its base. Guy Ballard once claimed to have met the alchemist Comte de Saint-Germain while hiking here, an event that prompted the formation of the "I AM" Activity movement, and poet Joaquin Miller frequently wrote about this peak and spent years living with the Native Americans near it. The second highest peak of the ► Cascades is, which stratovolcano of northern California?

One of this archipelago's islands includes Ses Paisses, a Bronze Age village which contains many megaliths called Talaiots, and another island contains a tomb called Naveta des Tudons. A cave at Es Culleram in this archipelago was the site of a shrine to Tanit, and important ancient cities here included Ciutadella and Mao or Mago. This archipelago's capital contains a sports arena that once hosted a Roger Federer match that was conducted on a half clay, half grass court, the so-called "Battle of the Surfaces", and its "Privilege" is recognized by Guinness as the world's largest nightclub. The author of a 1283 novel about a young man who becomes pope titled Blanquerna was born here. Besides Ramon Llull, this polity was also the birthplace to Federer's opponent in the aforementioned match, ► Rafael Nadal. The Pine and Gymnesian island chains are its two main groups, and this archipelago has deep cultural connections with Catalonia, which is located to its north. With capital at Palma, identify this autonomous community consisting of Ibiza, Menorca and Mallorca, islands off the east coast of the Spanish mainland.

One river that runs through this state is the Chaloosa, whose valley was explored by Father Emilie Fauthoux in the mid 1700's, while another geographical landmark is the Tonawanda Hills. This state's notable feats in education include sporting the first university in the world to ever conduct extension courses by radio. Lesser known cities in this state include Catawba, Galop de Vache, and Mohalis, while important architectural landmarks include the thirty-five story tall Second National Tower. While this state's most important city was founded in 1792, it did not enjoy mass settlement until the 1860's. Politicians who hailed from this state include Lucas Prout, while the powerful Revelation Motor ► Company was founded in this state as well. Taking its name from a Potawatomi word for "catfish," better known residents of this state include Seneca Doane and the former Fran Voelker. Identify this Midwestern state, which contains the sprawling city Zenith, the setting of such novels as Dodsworth, Arrowsmith, and Babbitt, and, of course, was created by Sinclair Lewis.

A 2004 book by John Mendelsohn and Selma el Obeid is subtitled The Flow of a Lifeline, and is titled after this body of water. The Popa Falls lie on this river, while the city of Maun near its delta is known as its nation's capital of tourism. Inhabitants of this river's delta were forced to flee across the Khwai River during the 1960s when its Moremi Game Reserve was designated a national park, and it provides water to Lake Ngami. Much of this river's water is eventually discharged into the Boteti River, which itself flows into the Makgadikgadi Pan. For 20 points, identify this river of Angola, Namibia and Botswana that empties into its namesake delta in the Kalahari Desert, thus never making it to the ocean.

The rail lines in this city divide into roughly three sections known as "Inner Way", "Outer Way" and "South Mound" and its name comes from a word meaning "place for drying fishing nets". One district in this city contains Hongbo Square as well as the Ji Le Temple and this city's is noted for its namesake Institute of Technology, opened in 1920, that was once known as the "Cradle for Engineers". This city's Daoli District contains its central Zhong Yang Street and this city is famous for its International Ice and Snow Scultpure Festival that resumed in 1985 following the Cultural Revolution. Lying on the Songhua River, for 15 points, identify this capital of the Heilongjiang Province, known as the "Oriental Moscow", a city in Northeastern China.

The Zig Zag and the Jenolan Caves are popular attractions in a mountain range of this name, and this color is sometimes used to describe a city home to Umaid Bhawan Palace, India's Jodhpur.Â Another city named for this color is being built off the coast of Muscat in Oman.Â A parkway with this color in its name passes through a namesake mountain chain, begins in Waynesboro and connects the Shenandoah and Great Smoky National Parks. A river with this color in its name flows past the Choke Mountains, gets water from the Rahad and Dinder rivers, and flows from Lake Tana in Ethiopia before ► joining with another colored river in Khartoum.Â name this color which also is present in a section of the Appalachians stretching from Pennsylvania to Georgia, and a river which joins with the White Nile.

A dispute over the ownership of a tract of land in this city was the basis for the 1899 Supreme Court Case Malony v. Adsit, which was presided over by this city's first mayor, Arthur Delaney. Cope Park, Wickersham State Historical Site, and Perseverance Theater are sites found within this city, whose namesake and co-founder is buried within its Evergreen Cemetery. The historic site of Fort Durham is located near the mouth of the Taku River, which empties into Stephens Passage at the southern end of this city. Formerly known as Rockwell and Harrisburg, it is located at the mouth of the Mendenhall River and its downtown area can be viewed from the top of Mount Roberts. Separated from Douglas Island by the ► Gastineau Channel, this city became a capital in 1906 after being moved here from Sitka. Identify this northernmost state capital of the United States.

Medieval kingdoms here included Gallura, Torres and Arborea, the latter of which was defeated at the 1409 Battle of Sanluri by Martin I. Among the mountainous terrain of this island, dominant architectural structures include the distinctive nuraghe, round prehistoric towers that provided fortification, including an extensive nuraghic village located near Dorgali. This island's highest peak is Mount La Marmora, located in the Gennargentu Massif, and the principal rivers on this island include the Tirso and Flumendosa. Scrub grasslands called maquis or macchia cover much of this island's countryside, which is dotted with cities including Nuoro, Orisanto and Sassari. The Campidano plain is the main agricultural region, and is where the capital of ► Cagliari is located. Name this large Mediterranean island separated by the Strait of Bonifacio from Corsica and by the Tyrrhenian Sea from mainland Italy.

This country's oldest National Park, Henri Pittier, is found within its state of Aragua, which forms the eastern shoreline of this country's third largest lake, Valencia. This nation's Dunes of Coro is its only desert, and the Cariaco Basin is located off its coast. Part of the border with its western neighbor is formed by the Arauca River, which meets with this country's chief river in the state of Apure. This nation was the home of revolutionary Francisco de Miranda, and the Battle of Carabobo led to its independence. Home to the Cordillera de la Costa and Cordillera de Merida ranges, the latter of which contains this country's highest point, ► Pico Bolivar, this nation borders the Gulf of Paria and contains a majority of the Guyana Highlands. Identify this South American nation home to Angel Falls and Caracas.

Remains of a Therapod discovered on one island named for this man were given the nickname "Naze" because of their discovery on the peninsula of that name. One land feature named for him expands from the Edward VII Peninsula to an anchor on one of his namesake islands, which itself is located in Graham Land and is separated from the mainland by the Prince Gustav Channel. A dependency named for this individual contains Williams Field and the Italian facility of Zucchelli Station, although it is owned by New Zealand. A ► sea named for this individual is bounded by Cape Colbeck, Cape Adare and Victoria Land, and is an extension of the southern Pacific Ocean.Â Discovering many of his namesake features leading an expedition on the HMS Erebus and HMS Terror, he also names an island in McMurdo Sound.Â name this British explorer who gives his name to the largest ice shelf in Antarctica.Â

The destination of 1975's Green March, following the deployment of MINURSO here, the Houston Agreement and Baker Plan both attempted to settle the dispute over it, and a 2000-mile long structure known as The Berm has been built in this entity to limit attacks from neighboring countries. Until 1958, this territory's northern region, known as Saguia el-Hamra and containing the rich phosphate deposits at the Bu Craa mines, was politically separate from the southerly Rio de Oro region, located between Cape Blanco and Cape Bojador. In the 1970s, during a guerilla campaign against the two occupying nations, this territory was named the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic by the nationalist ► Polisario Front, and was subsequently recognized by the Organization of African Unity in 1982. As a result of the ongoing civil war, Mauritania withdrew its claims to this region in 1979, and Morocco has occupied it ever since. With its colonial capital at Laayoune, identify this territory in northwestern Africa named for its location relative to a large desert.

In November 2006, Basil Watson unleashed his sculpture Balanced at the Doctor's Cave Beach resort in this country, the center of which can be found in the Bullhead Mountains. The Troy-Windsor and Quickstep Trails, as well as the Barbecue Bottom Road, take travelers through its largely uninhabited Cockpit Country, most of which is found in Cornwall County. This island was the site of Tacky's War in the 18th century, and later, Samuel Sharpe led a slave rebellion here known as the Baptist War. The eastern part of this country is dominated by the Jim Crow Mountains, as well as another range containing its highest point, the ► Blue Mountain Peak. Containing the cities of May Pen, Ochos Rios, and Spanish Town, this nation is bordered to the east by a namesake channel separating it from Hispaniola. Identify this Caribbean island nation, the site of Montego Bay and Kingston.

This area is home to the Zin River, which is found a short distance from the Ein Avdat, as well as Makhtesh Ramon, one of many large erosion craters unique to this region. Its eastern border contains the Arava Valley and it is home to the cities of Dimona and Arad, both of which were founded following the forced relocation of its native inhabitants to the Siyag. This region's cities of Nitzana, Shivta and Mamshit were founded by the Nabataeans, who ruled from nearby Petra, and its city of Rahat is home to a large Bedouin population. Described as a "desolation that not even imagination can grace with the pomp of life and action" by Mark Twain in The Innocents Abroad, this region contains the town of Eilat, which gives this region access to the Gulf of Aqaba. For 15 points, identify this region home to the town of Beersheba, a desert region of southern Israel.

A 2001 paper by Ilmar and Jonne Kotta discusses the "vertical migrations of mysids" in this body of water, whose name was lent to a mid-90s project that involved a phase studying the "structure of phytobenthic and associated animal communities" in this body of water. The German minesweeping torpedo-boats T-52, T-58, and T-46 were destroyed in a World War I operation with the intent to enter this body of water, which is fed by the Salaca, Gauja and Lielupe rivers. Bordering the Sorve Peninsula, this body of water contains the islands of Kihnu and Ruhnu, and is connected to its larger neighbor via the Muhu Sound and Irbe Strait. Found southeast of the island of ► Saaremaa, on its shores one can find the cities of Kuressaare, Parnu, and Jurmala, while its namesake city lies on the Western Dvina or Daugava River. Identify this arm of the Baltic Sea which takes its name from the capital of Latvia.

Reservoirs found within this state include the Alcova, Pathfinder, and Fontenelle, and it also contains the headwaters of the Belle Fourche River, which exits the northeast part of this state through its Crook County. Home to Curt Gowdy State Park and Medicine Bow National Forest, this state's capital is located next to the F.E. Warren Air Force Base at the junction of Interstates 25 and 80, the latter of which takes travelers by the cities of Green River and Rock Springs. The Bridger Wilderness Area is home to its highest point, ► Gannett Peak, and this state also features the first declared U.S. National Monument. The source of the Snake River and location of Jackson Hole, this is, what western U.S. State, home to Devils Tower, the Grand Tetons, and Old Faithful?

A 150 mile race created by Paul Every and nicknamed C2K sees its finish line at this location, which can be found in a namesake national park also containing the Talbingo and Tantangara Reservoirs. The journey to this place will take one by Seaman's Hut and Rawson's Pass, the latter of which is accessible from both Thredbo and Charlotte's Pass. This peak's name was transposed onto that of another when it was found out that nearby Mount Townsend was actually higher, and in 1997, a letter was officially added to its name so that it would coincide with the spelling of its namesake, whose name adorns this summit because Paul Edmund ► Strzelecki thought it resembled a namesake mound found in Krakow, Poland. Found in the Snowy Mountains of the Great Dividing Range, this is, what highest peak of Australia?

Drunken Point is a promontory found at the southern end of this body of water, on whose shores one can find the cities of Camp Morton and Victoria Beach. Also bordering a town nicknamed "The Capital of New Iceland," Gimli, this body of water's extensions include the Kinwow, Washaw, and Sturgeon Bays, the latter of which is connected to Lake St. Martin by the Dauphin River. Other tributaries include the Bloodvein and Poplar rivers, as well as a namesake river that flows north into this body of water from the Norman Dam located at Kenora. Found in the northeast part of what was formerly the prehistoric ► Lake Agassiz, it is drained by the Nelson River and fed by the Red River of the North, which flows through a namesake capital city found less than 40 miles south of this lake. Identify this Canadian lake sharing its name with the capital of Manitoba.

One colonial power forced the surrender of the Kingdom of Gowa on this island through the Treaty of Bongaya, and after World War Two, Captain "Turk" Westerling waged a bloody campaign here. The area around lakes Tempe and Sidenreng in the Walennae Depression serves as the center of this island's Bugis people, and it is also home to the Toraja ethnic group. 2000 saw the creation of the Gorontalo province from this area's namesake North province, which holds dominion over the Talaud and Sangihe islands located northeast of this place. Its deepest lake, Lake Matano, can be found in its South province, which is also the location of its two highest peaks: Mounts Rantekombola and Rantemario. Its longest river, the Lairiang, flows through the Bada Valley on the way to the strait that borders its west side and is named after its largest city, ► Makassar. Gulfs that border this island include Bone, Tolo, and Tomini, while seas that border this island include the Banda, Flores, Molucca, and a namesake sea to the north that separates it from the Philippines. Name this island, the fourth largest in Indonesia, also known as Celebes.

Forests in this region include the reed beech forest in its Hainich National Park as well as another, which contains the Rennsteig Path and cities like Friedrichroda and Oberhof, home to a large bobsled track.Â A landgrave of this region, Henry Raspe, was elected the German anti-king by Innocent IV in 1246, while earlier it was controlled by Louis the Bearded and the Ludowing family. A popular domestic tourist site in this state contains museums devoted to Frtiz Reuter and J. S. Bach, as well as ► Wartburg Castle, where Martin Luther famously translated his Bible. Besides Eisenach, other cities in this state include Meiningen, Gera and Jena. One of its cities was site to a constitution drafted by Hugo Preuss and signed by Friedrich Ebert in 1919.Â With capital at Erfurt and surrounded by the states Bavaria, Lower Saxony and Hessen, name this state of central Germany home to the city of Weimar.

This nation's Bay Islands Department has its capital at Roatan and is the home of a group of three islands from which a namesake pirate radio station operated in the 1960s in support of the Bay of Pigs invasion and against Castro; that radio station was later renamed Radio Americas. This nation is separated from its western border by the Motagua River, while its endpoint is Cape Gracia a Dios. This nation's southern shoreline includes its city of San Lorenzo, which lies on the Gulf of Fonseca, and along with its southeastern neighbor it shares the ► Mosquito Coast. Name this nation with capital at Tegucigalpa.

This river is home to the dam with the largest spillway gates in the world, the Masjed-Soleyman Dam, as well as the Gotvad Dam. A UNESCO World Heritage Site which lies on this river is the "Band-e-Kaiser," or Caesar's Dam, which was supposedly constructed by the army of the Roman Emperor Valerian after its defeat at the hands of Shapur I. This river originates in the Zard Kuh mountains of the Zagros Range and flows through Khuzestan. Along with the Tigris, Euphrates, and Karkheh, it is believed to be one of the four rivers of Eden in the Bible, being identified with the Pishon. The city of Basra was forced to declare a state of emergency after dams built on this river raised the salinity level of the Shatt-al-Arab. For 20 points, name this only navigable river of Iran.

This city is home to the thirty meter tall Alyosha Statue commemorating its heroism in the Second World War as well as to the Church of the Savior-on-the-Waters. This city is home to the world's northernmost Jewish synagogue, as well as a monument to Anatoly Bredov. Along with Churchill, this city is home to one terminus of the Arctic Sea Route. This city's namesake administrative region is home to Severomorsk, which is home to its nation's Northern Fleet, and this city is home to the world's only fleet of nuclear powered icebreakers. This city is located on the northern shores of the Kola Peninsula. For 15 points, name this largest city north of the Arctic Circle, located in Russia.

The Attali Commission supported the elimination of these administrative divisions which are led by a general council elected for six years. One location which recently became one of these entities consists of the islands of MahorÃ© and Pamanzi and has its capital at Mamoudzou. That example of a location which became one of these entities lies in the Comoros islands and is Mayotte. In addition to Mayotte, examples of these entities include the most populous one, which has its capital in the city of Lille; that example of these entities is ► Nord. Name these entities which have their seats of government in prefectures, administrative divisions of France which lie between the region and arrondissement levels.

This desert was the site of the wreckage of the bomber Lady Be Good, the crew of which believed they were only a few kilometers away from the sea and travelled northwest into this desert to die of thirst. This desert is the origin of a green crystalline substance used in Tutankhamun's jewelry which is believed to be the result of meterorite impacts; that substance is this desert's namesake "glass." This desert's eastern portion is known as the Western Desert and it is home to Wadi Sora, which inspired the "Cave of the Swimmers" depicted in the film The English Patient, as well as basin known for its salt flats, the ► flooding of which was, according to Bruce Arthur, proposed by the CIA. Name this desert home to the Qattara Depression, named for the country which is the site of Misrata and Benghazi.

This mountain's height was surveyed in 2004 by Damien Gildea's Omega Foundation. The first team to climb this mountain was led by Nicholas Clinch, and this mountain is part of a range which also includes Mount Shinn and Mount Tyree; that range is the Sentinal Range. This mountain is bordered by Goodge Col and the Branscob Glacier to its northwest, and it is linked to its southeast to the Craddock Massif. This mountain is also bordered by Branscomb and Crosswell Glaciers. This mountain shares its name with the aircraft carrier which delivered the SEAL team which killed Osama Bin Laden; both are named after the ► Georgia congressman known as the "Father of the Two Ocean Navy." name this highest mountain in Antarctica.

One UNESCO World Heritage site in this province is a set of namesake circular earthen fortresses at sites such as Hekeng and Tianluokeng built by its Hakka people; those locations are this province's tulou. This province's coasts are home to Haitan Island, while it's is bordered on its north by the Wuyi mountains. This province is home to almost all speakers of the Pu-xian variant of its most common dialect, Min, the eastern version of which is also named after this province. This province's city of Xiamen was one of the first Special Economic Zones created by the nation this province lies in and was once known as Amoy, while Quemoy lies off of this province's coast. For 15 points, name this Chinese province with capital at Fuzhou, which lies across the Formosa Strait from Taiwan.

One of this river's tributaries flows past the village of Tuli as well as the gold mining town of Nyangabgwe, also known as Francistown. In addition to the Shashe River, this river's tributaries include a river which flows through the state of Mpumalanga and passes through the Lebombo Mountains as well as a namesake gorge before draining into the ocean at Xai-xai. This river, the main tributary of which is the Olifants, is formed by the confluence of the Marico River and the Crocodile River and has its southwestern terminus in Kruger National Park. It is noted for the presence of a large sandbar which prevents access by large ships except at high tide, a fact noted by this river's discoverer, ►Vasco de Gama. Name this second largest African river which drains into the Indian Ocean.

One ethnic group in this nation is known for an initiation ritual known as Yondo. That ethnic group, the largest in this nation, is the namesake of the capital of this nation's Moyen-Chari region, which is also home to its Tupuri people. This nation which is home to the Sara people is also the site of Moundou, which lies on a river which flows northwest to meet the Chari River. That confluence of the Logone River is home to this nation's capital, which is linked by a bridge to the city of Kousseri. That capital of this country is located southeast of this nation's best known feature, which is fed by the aforementioned rivers, but which has ► shrunk up to 95%. Name this country bordered on its west by a namesake lake, with capital at N'Djamena.

This island's southwestern coast is home to a National Park which is home to Doubtful and Dusky Sounds, while offshore lie the uninhabited islands of Secretary and Resolution. That National Park, Fiordland National Park, is located on this island which is home to the World Heritage Site of Te Wahipounamu, which surrounds a glacier which is the origin of the Waiho River. In addition to being home to the Franz Josef Glacier, this island is home to Lake Matheson, which formed in a moraine left behind by the Fox Glacier. This island is home to the University of Otago, its nation's first university; that university lies in this island's city of Dunedin. This island was struck by a magnitude 6.3 earthquake in ► February 2011 near its town of Christchurch and it is bordered to the north by the Cook Strait. Name this larger of the main islands of New Zealand.

The Klickitat people believed that this mountain was once a maiden pursued by warriors named Wy'east and Pahto, who brought down the neighboring Bridge of the Gods in their battle. That maiden, named Loowit, was supposedly transformed into this mountain which was called that by the Sahaptin. This mountain's shape was influenced by the Kalama and Goat rocks periods and it is located in Skamania County. This mountain can be reached by the Spirit Lake Memorial Highway, which has its eastern terminus at this mountain which is also the site of Crater Glacier. This mountain is west of Mount Adams, and the most famous event at this mountain claimed the life of ► David A. Johnston. Name this Washington state volcano which erupted in May 1980.

This city's New Church is the site of a mausoleum designed by the de Keyser brothers. That mausoleum in this city is the burial site of a leader killed by the Balthazar brothers, and as a result, became of the burial site of all of his descendents, including Queen Juliana and Prince Bernhard. In addition to being the site of the tomb of William the Silent, this city was known for a type of tin-glazed pottery painted a namesake blue and was the predominant producer of roofing tiles in its home country in the 17th and 18th centuries. One depiction of this city shows a narrow arched doorway with a woman in a white bonnet and brown dress seated within it while in the center a woman in a red shirt and blue dress leans over a broom in another doorway. Another depiction of this city by the painter of The ► Little Street shows boats anchored on a waterfront across a river from figures in white and black as well as a canal running through this city. Name this city viewed in a painting by Jan Vermeer.

This archipelago was the site of the largest underground nuclear tests ever conducted the United States, which took place on Amchitka Island. This island chain contains the most diverse seabird colony in the Northern Hemisphere located on Buldir Island, and this island chain's largest city is located in a subgroup of islands which divides this island chain's West Census Area and East Borough. That subgroup, the Fox Islands, is also home to the tallest mountain in this island chain, the Makushin Volcano. That volcano lies on Amaknak Island in this island chain, which was once known as ► Dutch Harbor. Name this island chain home to Attu.

This city lies next to the Pongo de Mainique, which is a series of rapids carved by the Urubamba River, which seperates this city from the town of Aguas Calientes. Locations in this city include the Intihuatana stone, nicknamed the "Hitching Post of the Sun" as well as the zones of the Amautas and Ã‘ustas, the latter of which has trapezoidal doorways. Those locations lie in the three zones of this city, the Sacred District, the Popular District, and the District of the Priests and Nobility. This city's first discoverer donated much of what he found to ► Yale University, which has resulted in controversy with the country in which this city lies. Name this location discovered by Hiram Bingham, the most famous Inca city.

A location similar to this one seventy five miles to the west near Carondelet was destroyed to construct the nearest major city to this location; the only remaining part of that location is named Sugarloaf. This site is home to a location where an individual was buried with thousands of discs in the shape of a falcon surrounding him, an example of this location's "birdman" motif. In addition to that location, which also contained sacrificial victims and numbered seventy-two, one site at this location is the Grand Plaza, which was originally surrounded by a stockade along with this location's ► Monks site. That latter location at this site is also home to a site which shares a name with a similar place in England; that site is Woodhenge. Name this complex of mounds east of St. Louis.

This region's native inhabitants, who ate the pitahaya cactus, were the Cochimi people. This region is comprised of four deserts: the San Felipe, the Central Coast, the Vizcaino, and the Magdalena Plain. It was discovered in 1533 by FortÃºn JimÃ©nez. Its highest point is Pichado del Diablo, part of the Sierra de San Pedro MÃ¡rtir. Among the towns in its southern portion are its first capital, Loreto, and Santa RosalÃ-a, which features a church designed by Gustave Eiffel. Other cities in this region include ► Ensenada, Playas de Rosarito, and Tecate. Name this peninsula on Mexico's western coast with largest city Tijuana.

The highest mountains on this island are found in the Cerros del Macanao. Although not its capital, Porlamar is its chief city and Pampatar is its chief port. Among the most prominent beaches are Playa El Agua and Playa Puerto Cruz. Playa el Yaque is popular among windsurfers. In 1561, it was taken over by Lope de Aguirre, a notoriously vicious conquistador. Its defenders fought off Spanish forces in 1814, and Simon Bolivar was based here for one year in 1816 and drove off the Spanish general Pablo Morillo the next year. It is the main island of Nueva Esparta Province and has its capital at La Asuncion. For 20 points, name this island, the largest in Venezuela.

The largest settlement in this region was founded by Nabalco at Nhulunbuy to operate a bauxite mine, in a move opposed by the Yirrkala bark petition of 1963. One river in this region is traversed by Cahill's Crossing near the Ubirr rock art site. A national park in this region is home to the Ranger uranium mine. A river system in this region contains Twin and Jim Jim Falls; that river system is the Crocodile River. Part of Kakadu National Park is in this region, and notable residents of it include the Yolngu. For 15 points, name this region of Australia's Northern Territory, a site of Aboriginal autonomy that shares its name with a Dutch city.

Two examples of this landform, Cayos de Albuquerque and Cayos Este Sudeste, are located east of Nicaragua but claimed by Colombia. The Ralik Chain contains several of these landforms, which are also the location of the Reagan Test Site at Meck Island. One of these landforms used to contain Bokonijien, Aerokojlol and Nam, which were located near the Bravo Crater. Aldabra, Rennell, and Kwajalein are instances of these structures which also make up the ► Tuamotu and Caroline Islands. Charles Darwin suggested that the genesis of these structures occurs as a volcanic island sinks and coral reefs build up around it. Name these structures consisting of coral islands surrounding a lagoon, one of which was the site of the first hydrogen bomb test.

In 1924 Lewis Spence wrote that this island's blood was identical to that of the Iberians, and that a migration of Cro-Magnons from this island to Scotland had endowed Britain with "the greatest poets who ever touched the harp." The eastern side of this island faced Gaderius, and in its central plain a royal palace sat on a large hill, surrounded by concentric moats, which were later connected to the ocean by a canal. This island was abundant in natural resources, including a supply of orichalcum and a large population of elephants. In the center of the palace was a temple covered with silver, an ivory roof, golden pinnacles, and a large statue of six winged horses hitched to the chariot of ► Poseidon. The island of Santorini is one proposed candidate for this place. An impassible mud shoal existed on the site of what land destroyed by an earthquake, according to the dialogues Timaeus and Crito?

One book about this city discusses the Grange's efforts to form cooperatives here and analyzes its economic dominance by looking at regional bankruptcy filings. That book by William Cronon examines civic boosters like William Ogden in discussing "Second nature" and is titled Nature's Metropolis. Much of the white pine logged in Michigan's Cutover district was shipped to this city, and the Munn decision was based on grain elevators in this city. This city's Packingtown was home to a institution on ► Halstead Street that dumped into Bubbly Creek, and this city's namesake river's flow was reversed into the Sanitary and Ship Canal. Name this city, home to the union stockyards and a number of Louis Sullivan buildings.

One structure near this route has a copy of a Sefano Maderno scultpture of St. Cecilia. That catacomb of St. Callixtus is near this route, which was notably avoided during Operation Shingle. This route leaves one terminal city through the Porta San Sebastiano and connects that city to Capua. One structure built near this route has a window through which the Tomb of Caecellia Metella can be seen. Another building near this route contains footprints in stone and is the church of Domine Quo Vadis. A canal paralleling this route was built through the ► Pontine Marshes. The followers of Spartacus were crucified along what road that runs from Rome to Brindisi?

A civil war battle named for a tributary of this river saw Lew Wallace hold a position on the Georgetown pike. One manmade structure paralleling this river notably had a very large Inclined Plane and still has the Paw Paw tunnel. That structure, whose aqueduct Jubal Early tried to blow up, was superseded by the B&O railroad and is the C&O canal. This river crosses the fall line above Mather Gorge at Great Falls. The ► Blue Ridge has a water gap on this river where a tributary that passes through Front Royal enters this river. That tributary's namesake valley was fought in by Phillip Sheridan and enters this river at Harpers Ferry. The Shenandoah is the largest tributary of what river that forms the southern border of Maryland?

In 2010, the Gallup-Healthways Well-Being Index placed this city's quality of life at 161 out of 162 American cities; only Huntington, West Virginia fared worse. This city features a statue at George Lucas Plaza commemorating the movie American Graffiti, which was predominantly set here. It's home to its namesake Nuts, a minor league Colorado Rockies affiliate, as well as the largest winery in the world, the E & J Gallo. Found in Stanislaus County, this city's major newspaper, like other Central Valley cities Fresno and Sacramento is named the Bee. For 15 points, name this California city that may have been named for a personality trait of financier William Ralston when he declined to have this city named in his honor.

This desert contains brackish salt flats in the Umm al Samim region and featured a high concentration of shallow lakes from about 10,000 to 5000 years ago. It has seen its fair share of British explorers, including Bertram Thomas who was the first European to cross it, and Ranulph Fiennes who discovered the lost city of Iram here. Caravans used to cross this desert, but stopped around 300 AD. Due to increasing desertification which disrupted the ► frankincense trade that had traversed it for centuries. More recently, the oil field of Shaybah was opened on its northern edge by Aramco in the 1990s. Name this sand desert of the Arabian Peninsula also known as the Empty Quarter.

This mountain was first summited in 1800 by a party led by the brothers Sepp and Martin Klotz. It lies some 30 kilometers northwest of the city of Lienz and the view from the top of it on a clear day stretches from the Ortler in the West to Triglav in the east. The Pasterze Glacier lies at its base along a heavily traveled road named for this mountain which also contains the phrase "Hochalpenstrasse." It lies in the center of the Hohe Tauern and on the border of Carinthia and Tyrol, near where both of those states border the state of Salzburg. For 15 points, name this mountain, the second most prominent in the Alps by relative height and which since 1919 has been the highest in Austria.

In 1115, Conrad III was appointed Duke of this region by Henry V of the Holy Roman Empire. Ansbach, Schweinfurt, and Rothenburg ob der Tauber were part of the eponymous "Circle" of this region founded in 1500. This region is bounded topographically by the Spessart in the west and the Fichtelgebirge in the east. Lower, Middle, and Upper districts with this name form three of the seven Regierungsbezirke of the German state where most of this region is located. Small parts of this region, however, are located in Thuringia and Baden-WÃ¼rttemberg as well. For 15 points, name this region that contains the cities of WÃ¼rzburg and Nuremburg and the northern third of Bavaria.

A struggle between the Flynns and the Dorans for control here led to an 1899 gunfight. Ten casinos were located here during the Great Depression, which led Al Capone, Owney Madden and other mobsters to use it as a safe haven. This city also served as one of the first spring training camps with teams staying at the Arlington Hotel. Other travelers came here to visit America's smallest National Park. During 1862, the government of the state this city is in was also relocated here for a few months after the Battle of ► Pea Ridge. Bathhouse Row is in what resort town, the childhood home of Bill Clinton in central Arkansas?

One lake in this location is the pelican nesting site at Lake Elmenteita. Another body of water contains the soda lake fish Oreochromis and is fed by the Njoro River. That body of water attracts hundreds of flamingoes due to its high algae presence. One lake in this region has corrosive water due to high magnesium deposits and has a red color, due to the present of sodium carbonate runoff from the nearby volcano Ol Doinyo Lengai. This region contains Lake ► Nakuru and Lake Natron in addition to larger bodies of water, such as. Lakes Kivu, Edward, and Albert. Name this north-to-south running geologic formation in East Africa?

The only road running through this region runs over a series of wooden bridges from Pocone to Porto Jofre, though it was planned to run to the city of Corumba. This region is bounded by the Chiquitano forests to the northwest and by the cerrado plains to the northeast. Threats to the vitality of this region include coffee plantations called fazendas and gold mining operations that would bleed mercury into the water. This region is located mostly in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, and it covers an expanse of roughly 70,000 square miles. For 15 points, identify this region shared between parts of Brazil, Bolivia, and Paraguay, the world's largest wetland.

This province is the site of the Aspotogan and Chebucto Peninsulas, which bound its St. Margaret's Bay. Alexander Graham Bell Historic Park is located in this province, which contains the city of Truro at the edge of Cobequid Bay. The Digby Gut is a channel off of the Annapolis Basin that juts into this province. One island controlled by this province is separated from the mainland by the Strait of Canso and contains the city of Baddeck, which is the starting and ending point of the Cabot Trail. This province is connected to the mainland through the Isthmus of Chignecto, and it includes the cities of Peggy's Cove, Yarmouth, and Sydney as well as ► Cape Breton Island. Identify this Canadian province bordering the Bay of Fundy, formerly known as Acadia that has capital at Halifax.

This archipelago is the site of the Million Dollar Month fishing competition as well as Pirate Week in October. This archipelago's capital is known as Hog Sty Bay, and tourist attractions in this archipelago include the picturesque Seven Mile Beach and limestone formations called Hell. This archipelago was originally named "Las Tortugas" after the number of turtles seen, it is home to a notable Turtle Farm. It is also known for its stingrays, which can be viewed and touched in its Stingray City. ► identify this three island archipelago that has capital at George Town, a British dependency located south of Cuba in the Caribbean Sea named for a type of alligator.

This peak is located just south of the Traveler Mountain Range and it is the highest mountain in its state after Sugarloaf Mountain. This peak can be accessed by the city of Caribou to the northeast, and traditionally the area around this peak was inhabited by the Abenaki Indians. The Hundred-Mile Wilderness is a stretch of trail south of this peak, which is famous for an arete called the Knife Edge and is located in Baxter State Park. This peak is located on a divide which separates the West and East branches of the Penobscot River. The ► northern terminus of the Appalachian trail is located at, what highest peak of Maine?

This body of water received its name after a group of cliff's were named after the "great cloak" of the explorer Tia. This body of water is located south from Huka falls, and the large manmade Kaingaroa Forest borders the Eastern shore of this body of water, which also contains the fishing hotspot Tongariro National Park. The lake sits in the caldera of a supervolcano that erupted 26,500 years ago in the Oruanui eruption, and that volcano had activity as recent as 180 AD in the Hatepe Eruption. This body of water is located in the same political region as the glowworm caves of Waitomo. Drained by its country's longest river, the Waikato, and situated in the center of North Island, for 20 points, identify this lake, New Zealand's largest.

It's not in the Ukraine, but the highest peak in the central portion of this mountain range is called the Gates of Kiev. The world's largest zinc mine is the Red Dog Mine, located on the western edge of this range which serves as the source of the Chandalar River. Cities in this range include Wiseman and the truck stop Coldfoot. The village of Anaktuvuk is located in this range, which the Dalton Highway crosses through Atigun Pass. The highest peak in this range is Mount Chamberlain, and the Richardson Mountains are an extension of this range into the Yukon Territory. For 15 points, identify this mountain range running across northern Alaska.

According to the legend of the white hairpin, a woman whose husband had died decided to leap into this body of water rather than marry the emperor. This is commemorated by two black reefs past Shanhaiguan Pass. One site on this body of water is the Taoist sanctuary of Bijia Mountain connected to the mainland by the Tian Qiao and another location is the political retreat of Beidaihe. This body of water has an indentation at Laizhou Bay, and cities on its banks include Qinhuangdao in Hebei and Dalian. This body of water is enclosed by the Liaodong and Shandong Peninsulas and it contains the mouth of the Yellow River. For 20 points, identify this extension of the Yellow Sea, a gulf which stretches close to the city of Beijing.

This polity lost territory to the British in the Treaty of Sinchula after losing the Duar War, and this polity had governors called "ponlops" and a regent known as the Druk Desi. One ruler of this nation conquered the Lhapa kingdom and was referred to by the title "Shabdrung." That ruler received Portuguese Jesuit missionaries and unified this nation with his victory at the Battle of Five Lamas. Unified by Ngawang Namgyal, this nation's first king, Ugyen, signed a treaty in its city of Punakha, and the monarchs of this nation took a title meaning ► "Dragon King" and have all belonged to the Wangchuk royal family. Identify this nation which speaks a language called Dzongkha, a Buddhist kingdom located in the Himalayas with capital at Thimpu.

The resort towns of Langstrand and Dolfynstrand are located just north of this city. Attractions in this city include Sandwich Harbor and the offshore Guano Platform. The city is inhabited by ethnic Topnaars who lived in the Kuiseb River Delta, terminating in this coastal city which serves as an access point for Naukluft Park. The central dune belt near this city is home to Dune 7, a popular sandboarding location. This city was originally controlled by Britain during the scramble for Africa, and this city remained an enclave until 1994 after its nation gained independence in 1990 when it was governed by the Cape province instead of South-West Africa. For 15 points, identify this Namibian city formerly administered by South Africa whose name is Afrikaans for "Whale Bay."

Cities in this region include the coastal resort towns of Dahab, Nuweiba, and Taba. This region's northern portion contains the cities of Kakhl and Arish, and strategically important areas in this region include the Mitla Pass and the Gidi pass. The northwest corner of this area contains the Great Bitter Lake. One location in this region for named for a Christian martyr who was condemned to death on a wheel but was instead beheaded. Her head and hand are still present in this region's Saint ► Catherine monastery. The southern portion of this region borders the Straits of Tiran and Gubal and contains the resort city of Sharm el Sheikh. Bordering the Gulf of Aqaba and the Gulf of Suez, identify this triangle-shaped peninsula controlled by Egypt.

One location with this name is in an archipelago surrounding Manan Island but was left out of an 1817 catalogue of islands in Passamoquoddy Bay. That omission led to an ongoing dispute between the United States and Canada over that island in the Gulf of Maine. Another location with this name is located in False Bay and served as a communications outpost during World War II. That island is known for the high density of Great White Sharks in its surrounding waters. The Dutch name of Robben Island in Table Bay means "island of" these ► creatures. Identify this name associated with Machias Island, an island near Cape Town, and La Jolla beach, a type of pinniped from the family Otariidae which was featured in the 1994 children's movie Andre.

One early ruler of this territory was helped in a war against the Iban people by the British adventurer James Brooke. A 1962 uprising in this nation targeted oil resources in its city of Seria. This nation's only port city is Muara, and the city of Bangar is the capital of this nation's Temburong District. This nation's state ideology is the pro-Islam Melayu Islam Beraja, and this nation's seat of government is the Istana Nurul Iman, the world's largest palace. This nation claims ownership over part of the Spratly Islands and it is split in two by the province of Limbang. It has been ruled since 1967 by its wealthy ► sultan Hassanal Bolkiah. Identify this nation completely surrounded by the province of Sarawak in Malaysia, one of three countries on Borneo that has its capital at Bandar Seri Begawan.

The island of Caprera is located off the northern coast of this island and is accessible from the city of Palau, located near the resort tow of Porto Rotondo. Archeological sites on this island include Tharros, and a type of burial site called a "Giants' grave" can be found on this island and is attributed to its Bronze Age Nuragic culture. This island northern shore contains the glitzy Emerald Coast, and this island's central Gennargentu Range contains its highest peak, Punta La Marmora. Cities on this island include Olbia and its capital on a namesake gulf called the Gulf of the Angels and was known to the Romans as Caralis. Containing the Tirso River, this island is located south of the Strait of ► Bonifacio and its capital is located at Cagliari. Name this second largest island in the Mediterranean after nearby Sicily.

Accounts of life on this island were made by the Scot J. Alan Thompson, whose three accounts included "Only the Sun Remembers." The political party LALIT was formed in protest of foreign control over this island. This island encloses Eclipse Bay and Rambler Bay, and many native inhabitants of this island were deported to nearby Peros Banhos in the early 1970s. Along with Speakers Bank and the Egmont Islands, this island is part of the Chagos Archipelago, which itself is of the same geologic formation as the Lakshadweep Islands. This island was discovered by Pedro Mascarenhas and received its name by mistake from a similarly named Portuguese traveler. Used as a stop off between the nearby ► Maldives and Mauritius, identify this island in the British Indian Ocean Territory that is the site of a joint U.S. And U.K. Military base.

Architect Carlos Ott designed the tower for the ANTEL corporation headquartered in this city. This city's namesake obelisk is located in a park renamed for former president Jose Batlle y Ordonez which also contains a sculpture of oxen pulling a wagon called La Carreta. Neighborhoods of this city include Pocitos and Buceo, and the Cabildo and the Palacio Salvo are buildings located in the Ciudad Viejo of this city. That area also contains its nation's oldest theatre, the Teatro Solis, which contains streets called 18 de Julio Avenue and Artigas Boulevard. The first World Cup Final took place in this city's Estadio Centario, and this city was supposedly named when explorers shouted "I ► see a mountain." identify this city located across the Rio de la Plata from Buenos Aires, the capital city of Uruguay.

The semi-precious mineral Blue John is only found in this mountain range's Blue John cavern and Treak Cliff Cavern near the city of Castleton. One national park in this range is thought to be the world's second most visited after Mount Fuji. That park contains Dark Peak in its north and White Peak in its South and contains a feature called Thor's Cave in its Manifold Valley. The Cheviot Hills is a northern extension of this mountain range, which in other areas transitions into the Rossendale and Bowland Fells. This range is home to a namesake trail that extends from Edale to the city of Kirk Yetholm south of the Firth of Forth. The ► Peak District National Park in Derbyshire is the southern terminus of, what mountain range that forms the backbone of England?

One example of this geologic phenomenon is located north of Lake Gioleti in the middle of the Afar Depression and has existed for at least a century. The highest by altitude is located atop Villarica in Chile, though it may be subsiding. A third is located on Ross Island and contains an unusual amount of phonolite; that feature is part of a mountain that was the site of an Air New Zealand sightseeing crash and was originally named for the doomed companion of HMS Terror. For 15 points, there are only five extant examples of what landform involving molten rock that can be seen on Antarctica's Mount Erebus?

A suburb known as Al-Barid is located several miles north of this location and features notable frescoes of foliage, while Jabal Madhbah has a shrine to Dushara, the chief god of the people that created this location. Three large Djinn blocks are located next to a large obelisk at this location whose East Ridge has a structure named for a prominent Urn carved into it. A possible location of the tomb of Aaron is located southeast of this site, which also contains a number of Byzantine churches and a large Roman soldier graveland. A mountaintop in the northeast part of this location features al-Deir, or the Monastery, while visitors must walk through the narrow ► Siq before reaching the Treasury at the entrance. Identify this ancient Nabataean capital, a city of rock located in Jordan.

This river "turns up the grains of gold already tried" according to a poetic "farewell" to it written by Thomas Wyatt. This river's mouth contains the wreck of a ship that was carrying a full cargo of black pepper. The Embalsa de Valdecanas is a reservoir on this river that flows from a source in the Montes Universales. It divides regions known as the "Alen" and "Riba" with respect to this river, and either is or is not "more beautiful than the river that flows through my village" according to ► Fernando Pessoa. What longest river in Portugal flows into the Atlantic at Lisbon?
